item.title: 2 years of protests, one crucial election: Serbia's students challenge Vucic's 14-year rule
item.description: Serbia is gearing up for early parliamentary elections on October 25, which might alter the political scene significantly. Sparked by a catastrophic railway disaster in 2024, a student-led anti-corruption protest movement has gained momentum. Amid rising tensions, fears of government surveillance and the intimidation of political critics abound. With uncertainty surrounding the election outcome, both the ruling party and student activists brace for a closely contested battle.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Sasha Bogosian, 18, turns painted jeans into a nonprofit raising nearly $100,000 for kids' art therapy
item.description: Sasha Bogosian, an 18-year-old from Los Angeles, began painting denim after recovering from major surgery. Her artistic hobby evolved into The Sasha Project LA, raising funds for art therapy in children's hospitals. The project directly supports programmes that help alleviate children's pain and anxiety during treatment. Major brands like Levi's and BLICK Art Materials sponsor her initiative and contributions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Khosla ka Ghosla: Silicon Valley superstar's post for chief of staff sparks debate
item.description: Vinod Khosla has posted a job opening for a chief of staff at Khosla Ventures. The position requires intense work hours, typically from 8 am to 8 pm. Candidates are expected to have a strong commitment and be available nights and weekends. Khosla has emphasized the role's potential for learning and growth despite its demanding nature.

item.title: Historic Tucson tower gets a $50M affordable housing makeover
item.description: Tucson House in Arizona is undergoing a major renovation to provide affordable housing for older adults. The project is expected to create 358 modern apartments by summer 2028, improving accessibility for residents aged 55 and older. Twenty-five households have already moved into the newly renovated 15th-floor apartments within ten months of commencing work. Future updates will include shared amenities such as lounges, fitness rooms, and landscaped courtyards.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AI productivity plan backfires as task list hits 156
item.description: Morissa Schwartz's experience with her AI assistant revealed an unexpected outcome: an escalated to-do list. Instead of easing her tasks, the assistant generated more reminders and hurdles. To address this, she devised a plan to trim her task list and prioritize clear communication about challenges faced. Ultimately, Schwartz seeks to ensure her AI enhances her productivity rather than complicates it.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio couple spends $30,000 on friend's kitchen, loses legal battle to buy the house
item.description: An Ohio couple who moved into a friend's house in 2020 and spent $30,000 renovating its kitchen have lost their claim to purchase the property for $215,000. On Wednesday, an appeals court ruled that the renovations did not establish a binding purchase agreement. However, the couple may still receive compensation for the improvements, while the homeowners can pursue eviction proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2013, Amanda Seyfried bought a 1930s farm in Catskills; she converted the barn into a two-bedroom guesthouse and turned the property into a nonprofit animal rescue
item.description: Amanda Seyfried has rejuvenated a charming 1930s farm in the Catskills, turning it into a cozy family haven and a sanctuary for rescued animals. Not only did she expand the farmhouse, but she also transformed the barn into a delightful guesthouse. As a nonprofit animal rescue, they provide a home to various animals, including horses and dogs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bob Barker spent nearly $1 million to move three Toronto Zoo elephants to California; how Iringa, Toka and Thika found a new home
item.description: In a major win for animal welfare, three elderly elephants—Iringa, Toka, and Thika—have journeyed from Toronto Zoo to a sanctuary thanks to Bob Barker's generous funding of nearly $1 million. Their four-day trek concluded at the Performing Animal Welfare Society in California, where they will need time and veterinary expertise to adjust after decades of captivity. This move symbolizes hope for the future of the elephants and advocates alike.

item.title: Indian-origin siblings turn lemonade stand into nonprofit, donating books and helping 15,000 students
item.description: Rohan and Anya Satija initiated the Let's Learn Foundation to provide books and mental health support. They began their efforts with a lemonade stand in 2018, raising awareness about educational inequalities. The foundation has since reached over 15,000 students across Texas and partnered with various organizations for resources. Their mission continues to focus on underserved communities to ensure equitable access to education.

item.title: Trump, Putin, Xi could hold meeting in China; discuss end to Ukraine conflict: Moscow
item.description: A possible trilateral meeting involving Russian, US, and Chinese leaders could happen to discuss the Ukraine conflict. This meeting is suggested to take place during the upcoming APEC summit in China next month. However, Ukraine has expressed concerns about being excluded from such discussions. Ukrainian officials believe this exclusion may encourage Russian President Vladimir Putin to prolong the war.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Watch: Calm couple, unfazed jogger defy chaos on streets of France
item.description: France is currently facing significant protests driven by rising living costs and deteriorating public services. While some residents appear unfazed by the chaos, many cities have witnessed violent rioting and looting. The government has implemented tighter security measures after over 2,400 individuals were arrested during recent unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has suggested localised curfews to curb further violence.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 'Not accident': Australian PM says MP Helen Haines was hit in 'deliberate act'
item.description: Helen Haines, an independent lawmaker in Australia, was critically injured after being struck by a car. The incident occurred outside her electoral office and is being investigated as an apparent deliberate attack. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese condemned the act and mentioned that a driver was arrested at the scene. There was also a knife found inside the vehicle during the investigation.

item.title: Barbados-born man, 62, faces deportation after 50 years in Britain over a past criminal conviction
item.description: Tony Hall, a 62-year-old London resident, faces deportation despite living in the UK for 50 years. His immigration issues stem from a 2001 criminal conviction for conspiracy to rob and possession of a firearm. He has lived under a deportation threat for over 14 years, reporting biweekly to the Home Office. Hall's current status leaves him at risk of homelessness as he relies on his sister for support.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Buildings ablaze, petrol bombs hurled at parliament: 10 visuals show chaos of Albania protests
item.description: Protests in Tirana against Prime Minister Rama have escalated, marked by violent confrontations between crowds and law enforcement. Frustrated by rampant corruption and expensive university tuition, protesters have hurled stones and petrol bombs. In reaction, police have unleashed water cannons and tear gas to control the situation, resulting in multiple injuries on both sides. International organizations are urging for an immediate peaceful resolution to the mounting tensions.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan
